How many units are in a pint?

A pint of 4% lager is 2.3 UK units. Pick your drink and strength below to work out units, US standard drinks and Canadian standard drinks for anything you're drinking.

By the ontap team · 20 October 2026

How to work out units

One UK unit is 10 ml of pure alcohol. Multiply the strength by the volume in millilitres and divide by 1,000:

Units = ABV (%) × volume (ml) ÷ 1,000
4% × 568 ml ÷ 1,000 = 2.27, so about 2.3 units in a pint of ordinary lager.

Units in common pints

DrinkStrengthUK units
Pint of ordinary lager, bitter or cider4%2.3
Pint of premium lager5%2.8
Pint of strong lager or cider5.5%3.1
Pint of stout4.2%2.4
Pint of IPA6%3.4
Half pint of 4% lager4%1.1
440 ml can of 5% lager5%2.2

Units vs standard drinks

Countries count differently. The UK uses units (8 g of alcohol). The US counts standard drinks of about 14 g, like a 12 oz can of 5% beer. Canada's standard drink is 13.45 g (17.05 ml), like a 341 ml bottle of 5% beer. That's why a UK pint of 4% lager is 2.3 units but only about 1.3 US standard drinks.

How much is too much?

The UK Chief Medical Officers advise not regularly drinking more than 14 units a week, spread over three or more days, with some drink-free days. That's about six pints of 4% lager a week. If you want to keep an eye on it, a free tracker like MyDrinkaware is built for exactly that.

FAQ

How many units are in a pint of Guinness?

Guinness Draught is 4.2% in the UK, so a pint is about 2.4 units (4.2 × 568 ÷ 1,000).

How many units in a pint of 5% lager?

About 2.8 units: 5 × 568 ÷ 1,000 = 2.84.

Is a US pint the same as a UK pint?

No. A UK pint is 568 ml (20 imperial fl oz); a US pint is 473 ml (16 US fl oz), about 17% smaller.

How long does a unit take to leave your body?

Roughly an hour per unit for most adults, but it varies a lot from person to person, and nothing speeds it up. Never drive after drinking.
